findings.where: Lede under the 'How we rank' heading, and the 'Ranking method' section
findings.fault: The lede says the page 'states in full how a hostel's position is decided', but the page never says what sets the order. It explains how a score is computed and says review count is never the default sort. It never says what the default sort is (displayed score? something else?), or how 'information on record' such as distance or vibe affects position. 'Area' is also never defined. A reader finishes knowing how a score is made, not why one hostel sits above another.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker comparing two listings who wants to know why one ranks higher, and a hostel owner reached by cold outreach who wants to know what would move them up. Both came for exactly what the heading promises, and both leave without it. That undercuts the page's whole claim to openness.

findings.where: Last section, 'Hostelworld, for comparison', which closes the page
findings.fault: The page ends on a named competitor and suggests that Hostelworld's method makes small hostels 'look thin'. The brief positions Manta to name no competitor and never to compete on Hostelworld's ground. The founder is also waiting on Hostelworld's consent for an affiliate application. A visitor's last impression is a dig at an incumbent, not Manta's own method.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because a public critique of Hostelworld's scoring could harm the pending affiliate consent and breaks the 'names no competitor' positioning. A backpacker may also read the closing comparison as point-scoring, which weakens the calm, neutral tone a method page relies on.

findings.where: 'Ranking method', third paragraph (reviews that earn their writer a reward)
findings.fault: The page admits that reviews earn their writers a reward. It never answers the obvious objection: does the reward depend on the review being positive, or on what it says? Without that line, 'incentivised reviews' reads as 'paid reviews'.
findings.who_objects: A sceptical backpacker who has learned to distrust rewarded reviews. Without that reassurance the whole score is suspect, and that is the trust this page exists to build.

findings.where: Whole page: heading block and footer
findings.fault: The page gives no date. There is no 'last updated' or effective date for the method, and no copyright year. The only date on the page belongs to the Hostelworld source. A published method that can change, with decay rates stated as current fact, gives no sign of which version is in force.
findings.who_objects: A hostel owner or careful traveller checking the method later. They cannot tell whether it is current or whether it has changed since they last read it.

findings.fault: Every promise ('No hostel can pay for a higher position') is made by an unnamed 'we'. No name or one-line identity appears beside the method. The only trace of a person is the first name in the footer email. For a pre-launch product with no reviews, partners or press, the founder's name is the only credibility the page has to offer, and it does not use it.
findings.who_objects: A hostel owner hearing about Manta through cold B2B outreach, who wants to know who is making a payment-independence promise before trusting it. A traveller meeting an unknown brand for the first time has the same question.

findings.where: End of the content, above the footer
findings.fault: After the last section there is no next step. Nothing links back to destinations or invites a reader, now persuaded, to go and look at hostels. The only routes onward are the nav at the top and the footer links.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who arrived from a listing to check the ranking and is now ready to compare. On a phone they have to scroll all the way back up to the menu to carry on.
